correctness.rationale: For finite acyclic essential networks, the longest-source-path rank is invariant on vertex orbits and strictly increasing on quotient arcs. Arc-orbit selections have exactly equivalent marked path reachability by a direct lift. Barycentric coefficients on orbit vertices yield inverse PL maps between each geometric H-fixed set and the quotient path complex. Published Grinberg--Katthän--Lewis Theorems 1.9(b) and 1.10(b) give spheres for all quotient networks. Signed oriented simplex Lefschetz contributions depend only on the number of selected arc orbits, giving character det(Z[U]) for PF and det(Z[E]) tensor det(Z[U]) for PM. The formal degree-minus-one case is handled. Replayed executable verifier exhaustively checks 332 small essential DAGs, 405 automorphism actions and five subgroups of a 2-by-2 layered network; this supports, but is not substituted for, the proof.

value.rationale: The result gives an all-subgroups genuine fixed-space homotopy dimension function and explicit integral rank-one symmetry modules for an infinite family of essential acyclic two-terminal networks, not merely a new finite Betti count. The same network yields two sphere complexes with different orientation modules and contrasting rational top homology of symmetry orbit spaces. This supplies a structural equivariant extension of a natural published path-avoidance construction, while explicitly leaving equivariant homotopy splitting and general orbit-space integral topology open.
